title: Cottrell's style and Piron band's playing
summary: Frazier describes Cottrell as a snare-roll timekeeper, mentions the Temple Roof Garden crowd, and whether he took solos.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Go back to Contra. How did he play in this, uh, Huron band? You know, what sort of stuff did he play?

Oh, strictly, we call it professional drumming, you know? You didn't have all this, all these tum-tums, you know? No. It was strictly plenty of snare drumming, nice beats on the snare drum, and it's top-sender than these Chinese locks.
Hmm. Just more as a timekeeper, was he?

Timekeeper, yeah. A straight drum, dance, I don't know, they never say he was what you call a flash drummer, you know, to make all kind of breaks. Yeah. I never see him do it. He might, could have did it, but I never saw him.
But he used the same sort of snare drum rolls as you're using now.
Yeah, he was the first man to give you the ideas of that.
Did he, did he used to play on the cymbal, you know, beat on the cymbal going out?
Yeah. Yeah, he had a rhythm like that. Yeah. A light tap going out with that band, yeah. Mm-hmm. Yeah, he had a light tap.
Do you ever remember him taking these solos, you know, drum solos?

I don't remember the kind of old man knows. He might have did it, you know, because they was working mostly on these nightclub jobs, like at Spanish Folk, and one night they pull a big dance at the place they call the Temple Roof Garden, and they had his band, Piran band over there, and Manuel Perez band. Manuel Perez was the house band. Yeah. And the place, to claim there, a crowd of 2,100 people up there, that's a large crowd for a place like that. Did you? He could even have, all the heads standing room in there that night. I forgot what year and what month it was. The place was jammed. And, uh, I never see him take no drums or this thing, this regular straight rhythm, you know. Yeah, that's it, yeah. Yeah, but everybody recognized that. I was going to ask you, going back to Coachella again, huh?
You know they do drum tags on the end of things now? Yeah. Did he ever do anything like that? Did he ever do anything like that? Did he ever do anything like that? Did he ever do it?
I don't know. That band, you know that band had a different style of playing. But the old jazz band used to do it. Yeah, they'd make a tag. Did you ever hear them records they made?
Piran made some records, you ever hear them? Yeah, yeah, I heard lots of records of Piran bands.
Do you think it was a good example of how they played?
You know, were they playing like that? That sort of thing?
